Robot Doctor Mechanisms

Slides or arm sag, slip, or won't hold

Drops when you let go, creeps down, or can't hold height. Below are the 6 most common causes on FTC robots, ordered from most to least likely, with how to check and fix each one.

Skip the guesswork — run the interactive diagnosisAbout 6 quick questions narrow this list down to your robot's actual problem.

Quick checks first

  • Does it sag while the code is trying to hold it (not just when power is off)? Hold a position in code and watch whether it slowly drops.
  • Is the motor set to BRAKE zero power behavior? Search for setZeroPowerBehavior on that motor.
  • Does your control code add a gravity term (kG / feedforward)? A constant added to the output for slides, or kCos × cos(angle) for arms.
  • Is the string loose, frayed, or wrapped messily on the spool? Look at the string with the slide retracted and extended.
  • If you draw a marker line across the hub and shaft, does it split after running? Draw one straight line over the hub (or collar) and the shaft, run it a few times, and look again.
  • Does the chain or belt feel loose or sag in the middle? Press the middle of the run with a finger.

Common causes and how to fix them

1 No gravity feedforward

Gravity is a constant load. Without a feedforward term, PID has to fall below the target before it pushes back, so the mechanism sags.

How to fix it 20 min

  1. Vertical slides: add a constant kG to the output. Raise it until the slide just holds still at mid-height.
  2. Arms: gravity changes with angle, so scale the term by cos(angle), with 0° pointing horizontally.
  3. Then tune PID on top for the remaining error.
Feedforward + PID
// vertical slide
double power = pid.calculate(target, slidePos) + kG;

// arm (angle in degrees, 0 = horizontal)
double power = pid.calculate(target, armAngle) + kCos * Math.cos(Math.toRadians(armAngle));

Sources: GM0 · Control loops

2 Motor set to FLOAT when idle

The default zero power behavior lets a motor spin freely at 0 power, so gravity pulls slides and arms down.

How to fix it 2 min

  1. Set slide and arm motors to BRAKE. It shorts the motor leads and resists motion when power is 0.
  2. BRAKE helps, but it is not a hold. Heavy loads still creep down, so add a small holding power or feedforward too.
Brake when idle
slide.setZeroPowerBehavior(DcMotor.ZeroPowerBehavior.BRAKE);

Sources: GM0 · Common software issues · GM0 · Control loops

3 Slide string is slack, stretched, or mis-spooled

Loose string, string that stretched, or a spool that unwinds lets the slide drop, jump, or tangle.

How to fix it 20 min

  1. Re-tension: rig the extension string with the slide retracted and the retraction string with it fully extended (GM0).
  2. Clamp strings with a bolt instead of knots so you can re-tension quickly.
  3. Use the same spool diameter for extension and retraction in continuous rigging.
  4. With elastic retraction, watch for the spool unwinding past zero.
  5. Replace string that has stretched or frayed. Braided fishing line or Dyneema is the usual choice.

Sources: GM0 · Slide rigging

4 Hub or collar slipping on the shaft

Set screws work loose and chew the shaft, so the gear or sprocket spins while the shaft does not (or the reverse).

How to fix it 15 min

  1. Mark the shaft and hub with a marker line. If the lines separate after a run, it is slipping.
  2. Switch to clamping hubs and collars, or hex / D-shaft hubs, wherever possible.
  3. If you must use set screws, file a flat on round shafts and use blue threadlocker on metal (never on plastic).
  4. Use nylon locknuts everywhere. Plain nuts vibrate loose.

Sources: GM0 · Building tips · GM0 · Shaft retention

5 Chain or belt tension is wrong

Too loose and it skips teeth or falls off. Too tight and it strains the motor.

How to fix it 15 min

  1. Press the middle of the run. It should flex a little but not sag.
  2. Add an adjustable tensioner. Chain stretches over time, faster on small sprockets.
  3. Over-tightening burns out motors and wears bearings, so do not crank it.

Sources: GM0 · Chain · GM0 · Belt

6 Position control gains are off

Too much P makes it oscillate, too little leaves it short. D is what damps overshoot.

How to fix it 30 min

  1. GM0's tuning order: set I and D to 0, raise P until it oscillates around the target, then add D until the overshoot is gone.
  2. Oscillating around the target means not enough D. Reaching it very slowly means not enough P (or too much D).
  3. Leave I at 0 unless friction stops it short. If you use I, cap it so it cannot wind up.
  4. Use the RoboCodex PID tuner to get a feel for each gain before touching the real robot.

Sources: GM0 · Control loops
